reason: H0 exclusively instantiates wuffs_bmp__decoder and compiles WUFFS_CONFIG__MODULE__BMP, so it cannot reach the new Netpbm decoder. Consequently, S1's P5/P6 header and raster parsing, incremental short-read behavior, pixel swizzling, call_sequence transitions, and restart protocol receive no coverage. Even if the generic fuzz_image_decoder helper were reused later, its fixed decode sequence never calls restart_frame!, leaving the 0x28 restart state and #bad restart/#bad argument paths uncovered.
evidence: H0 defines WUFFS_CONFIG__MODULE__BMP and constructs wuffs_bmp__decoder; it contains no NETPBM module definition or netpbm decoder instance.
S1 adds pub struct decoder implementing base.image_decoder in std/netpbm/decode_netpbm.wuffs.
decoder.do_decode_image_config? recognizes P5 and P6 inputs and parses comments, width, height, and max_value, including limits up to 0xFF_FFFF and the required max_value of 255.
decoder.do_decode_frame? and decoder.swizzle! process attacker-controlled raster bytes incrementally and preserve dst_x/dst_y across $short read yields.
decoder.restart_frame! introduces a distinct call_sequence state 0x28, validated later by decoder.do_decode_frame_config? against frame_config_io_position.
fuzz_image_decoder only calls decode_image_config, decode_frame_config, decode_frame, workbuf_len, and frame_dirty_rect; it never calls restart_frame!.
recommended_action: Add a Netpbm-specific harness that enables the Netpbm module, initializes its decoder, and drives P5/P6 inputs through incremental and closed-input decoding. Extend protocol coverage to fuzz restart_frame! arguments and source-position handling, then resume decode_frame_config/decode_frame from the 0x28 restart state.
